title: Physical shape and material parameter gradients: slab thickness and permittivity against the Airy derivative, polygon vertices under mesh refinement

fixture.planar_slab: tests/test_gradient_mesh_slab.py via benchmarks/gradient_mesh.py: 2D domain 8 x 0.24 um, y periodic, slab thickness 0.23 um at x = 0.013 um with permittivity 2.25 in air, wavelength 1.55 um, one-cycle plane pulse at x = -1.5 um, transmitted and reflected normalized-flux planes at x = +-0.8 um, physical time 90 fs (time_step_override so that steps times dt is exact), CPML 0.4 um, float32 CUDA, DifferentiableSolid.box through smooth_geometry_epsilon of width w, 8 checkpoints; joint refinement (mesh, width) = (0.04, 0.16), (0.02, 0.12), (0.01, 0.08) um then the regularization followup (0.01, 0.06) um with actual improvement steps of 0.001 um and 0.01 in epsilon; fixed-width controls (0.04, 0.12) and (0.01, 0.12) um; duration control 120 fs and PML control 0.5 um at (0.01, 0.06) um
fixture.polygon_grating: tests/test_shape_gradients.py record docs/validation/shape_gradient_polygon_3060.json: pentagon of five off-grid vertices with epsilon 4 in a 4 x 0.6 um y-periodic domain, 60 fs, CPML 0.24 um, normalized transmitted flux at 1.55 um, checkpointed adjoint at (mesh, width) = (0.04, 0.08), (0.02, 0.08), (0.01, 0.08) and (0.02, 0.04), (0.01, 0.04) um in float32, float64 precision control, 90 fs duration control, 0.30 um PML control; reference central differences at mesh 0.005 um in float64 with steps 0.002 and 0.001 um for widths 0.08 and 0.04 um; sharp-interface forward runs (width 1e-9) at 0.01 and 0.005 um
fixture.geometry_maps: tests/test_differentiable_geometry.py: box centre, rotation and epsilon, cylinder radius and height, background epsilon through the fill VJP (float64, no FDTD) and an FP32 geometry-to-FDTD adjoint and streamed chain on 18 steps
fixture.pml: 0.4 um in the slab study with a 0.5 um control; 0.24 um in the polygon record with a 0.30 um control

precision: float32 CUDA for the slab and polygon adjoints
float64 for the polygon reference differences and the geometry map checks
backend: cpu for the record contract and geometry maps
cpu and cuda for the FP32 chain
reference_method: Closed-form Airy transmission T(d, epsilon) of an air/slab/air stack and its analytic derivatives dT/dd and dT/depsilon, checked against an independent complex-amplitude transfer formula by central differences (tests/test_gradient_mesh.py); for the polygon, central differences of the same regularised fill at a four times finer mesh (mesh convergence of the regularised derivative, not a sharp-interface shape derivative, as docs/SHAPE_GRADIENTS.md states).

observables.name: thickness_derivative_relative_error
observables.definition: |dT/dd - analytic| / |analytic| with the derivative per um

observables.name: conservation_error
observables.definition: |T + R - 1| with R from the incident-subtracted reflected plane

observables.name: improvement
observables.definition: predicted, actual and analytic change of T for a gradient step of 0.001 um in thickness and 0.01 in epsilon

observables.name: control_changes
observables.definition: changes of T, dT/dd, dT/depsilon when the duration goes 90 to 120 fs or the PML 0.4 to 0.5 um

observables.name: polygon_gradient_relative_l2
observables.definition: relative L2 of the ten vertex derivatives against the fine-mesh float64 central differences

acceptance.source_of_limits: completion_gates.json proposed_thresholds physical_parameter_gradient_relative_error_nonzero 0.03 for the slab followup and the polygon fine mesh; the slab's first 0.08 um width missed 3 percent (2.80 and 3.19 percent) and the 0.06 um followup is the declared fixture, kept in the record as the initial_validation note

tests/test_gradient_mesh_slab.py::test_s.oracle: Airy transmission and its thickness and permittivity derivatives; joint mesh/width refinement with duration and PML controls

tests/test_gradient_mesh.py::test_airy_d.oracle: oracle self-check against an independent complex-amplitude transfer formula

tests/test_gradient_mesh.py::test_refine.oracle: fixture invariants of the refinement (size, time, PML, source)

tests/test_shape_gradients.py::test_shap.oracle: stored polygon record: regularised vertex derivatives under mesh refinement against fine-mesh central differences (convergence_study of the regularised derivative)

tests/test_shape_gradients.py::test_vert.oracle: central differences of the same discretisation

tests/test_differentiable_geometry.py::t.oracle: checkpointed and streamed FP32 chain against full autograd

not_yet_covered: sharp-interface (staircase) shape derivative convergence: the polygon reference is the regularised fill at a finer mesh and the sharp forward runs carry no gradient
regeneration of the polygon record under pytest (the record is checked, not recomputed; python -m benchmarks.shape_gradient_polygon regenerates it on CUDA)
curved interfaces, rotated boxes and cylinder radii against an analytic derivative (checked against finite differences of the same discretisation only)
near-zero derivatives judged on a characteristic absolute scale (both slab derivatives are of order 0.2 to 0.3 and judged relatively)
asymptotic convergence order of the slab derivatives (docs/gradient_mesh.md: no order established)

error_budget.precision_floor: float32 adjoint; the polygon float64 control changed the gradient by 6.6e-7 relative and T by 4.4e-7, so float32 round-off is far below the 3 percent budget; the slab conservation error is 1.8e-5
error_budget.time_window: slab 90 fs with a 120 fs control (changes at most 1.8e-7); polygon 60 fs with a 90 fs control (gradient change 5.8e-6 relative)
error_budget.pml: slab 0.4 um with a 0.5 um control (changes at most 1.2e-7); polygon 0.24 um with a 0.30 um control (1.8e-6 relative)
error_budget.mesh_and_regularisation: slab joint refinement 12.1, 6.8, 2.8 percent (thickness) and 12.0, 7.0, 3.2 percent (epsilon) then 1.63 and 1.78 percent at width 0.06 um; polygon 11.6, 1.78, 0.51 percent at width 0.08 um and 5.4, 0.99 percent at 0.04 um

notes: tests/test_gradient_mesh_slab.py is added with this case as a thin wrapper of benchmarks/gradient_mesh.py whose checks were declared with docs/gradient_mesh.md and the stored record; the pilot at this commit reproduced 1.633 and 1.783 percent at the followup (T error 0.00229, conservation 1.8e-5, controls below 1.8e-7) in 95 s on the shared RTX 3060. The polygon record is checked by the existing contract test and not recomputed here.
